dnn_module.summary: New graph-based inference engine coexists with classic 4.x engine. Typed operation graph with shape inference, constant folding, operator fusion (including FlashAttention-style attention fusion), unified buffer pool. ENGINE_AUTO (default) tries new engine first then falls back; ENGINE_CLASSIC / ENGINE_NEW / ENGINE_ORT selectable via readNet* engine arg or OPENCV_FORCE_DNN_ENGINE env (1=classic, 2=new, 3=auto, 4=ORT).
dnn_module.onnx_coverage: Claimed jump from ~22–23% ONNX operators (4.x) to >80% (5.x); dynamic shapes, If/Loop subgraphs, QDQ quantize/dequantize graphs supported.
dnn_module.int8_fp16: Core adds first-class CV_16F (fp16/hfloat) and CV_16BF (bfloat16) plus CV_Bool, CV_32U/64U/64S. New engine supports QDQ quantized graphs. No claim that new engine natively runs all models as int8/fp16 kernels beyond QDQ + type support; new engine is CPU-only at 5.0.
dnn_module.gpu: New engine CPU-only at 5.0; GPU planned later. Workarounds: force classic engine (CUDA/OpenVINO targets) or build WITH_ONNXRUNTIME(+GPU).
dnn_module.arm_neon_perf: HAL vendor paths: Intel IPP/SSE-AVX, Arm KleidiCV (NEON/SVE/SME; validated AWS Graviton 4 & Cortex-A), Qualcomm FastCV, RISC-V RVV. Universal Intrinsics 2.0; blog claims 3–4× on common ARM ops (resize/warp). Phoronix: tuned paths for Arm KleidiCV among others.
dnn_module.llm_vlm: Built-in tokenizer + KV-cache; samples for VLMs/LLMs (Qwen 2.5, Gemma 3, PaliGemma, GPT-family) and LaMa/LDM inpainting.
dnn_module.removed_parsers: Darknet and Caffe parsers removed; convert to ONNX. TFLite still via classic engine.

face_apis_models.FaceDetectorYN_FaceRecognizerSF: No OpenCV-5 wiki/migration-guide claim of FaceDetectorYN / FaceRecognizerSF API breaks. Migration guide still recommends YuNet via FaceDetectorYN.create as modern replacement for Haar. 4.x and 5.x face_recognize.cpp still expose feature() + match() (cosine or L2 after L2-normalize); feature dim is model-defined (SFace ONNX forward).
face_apis_models.opencv_zoo_yunet_2026may: face_detection_yunet_2026may.onnx is default with dynamic H/W dims for OpenCV 5.x ORT engine (OPENCV_FORCE_DNN_ENGINE=4); re-export of face_detection_yunet_2023mar.onnx with symbolic dims. Also 2023mar fixed-shape + int8 block-quantized variants. License: MIT. Source train: libfacedetection.train (WIDER Face).
face_apis_models.sface: face_recognition_sface remains; Apache-2.0 zoo files; MobileFaceNet + SFace loss; int8bq variant present. No new 2026 SFace weights called out in zoo README.

migration_gotchas_4x_to_5x: Legacy C API fully removed (CvMat/IplImage/cvCreateMat etc.).
OpenVX support removed; G-API and classic ML moved to opencv_contrib.
features2d renamed features; Haar CascadeClassifier + HOGDescriptor → xobjdetect in contrib.
calib3d split → geometry / calib / stereo / ptcloud (C++ calib3d.hpp shim still works; Java imports change).
1D/0D Mat semantics: std::vector→Mat is true 1D (not Nx1); may break .rows/.cols assumptions.
New Mat types (BF16, Bool, 64-bit ints) — switch(mat.depth()) needs default.
DNN: Darknet/Caffe loaders gone; new engine CPU-only; GPU needs classic or ORT.
Imgproc: INTER_NEAREST matches Pillow; warp bilinear/bicubic numerically differ from 4.x; text rendering STB/Rubik (Hershey still API-compatible but looks different).

pipeline.detectors: Single DNN on full image outputs face and upper-body (torso) boxes; associate face↔body by area, position, intersection.
pipeline.embeddings: Separate face embedding network and upper-body embedding network produce feature vectors; same-person crops close, different far.
pipeline.combination_formula: D_ij = min(F_ij, α·F_ij + β·T_ij) where F is face distance, T upper-body distance. Face-only → compare to cluster mean face; body helps only if same moment; body-only → use body distance.
pipeline.when_torso_trusted: First-pass clustering compares upper-body embeddings only within the same "moment" (assets linked by time/location metadata) because clothing is assumed consistent same day/event. Second pass is face-only HAC across moment boundaries.
pipeline.clustering: Pass 1: conservative agglomerative clustering on combined face+body (high precision, many small clusters; running average centroids). Pass 2: hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) on face embeddings only (median linkage, sampling for scale). Gallery = K largest clusters via size/distance heuristics + user input.
pipeline.assignment: Sparse coding against dictionary of canonical exemplars per cluster (not pure nearest centroid); assign by max energy of sparse code.
pipeline.filtering: Uncertainty/confidence branch + OOD filters remove false positives and unclear faces/bodies before they pollute gallery.
pipeline.embedding_dims: NOT STATED in the Apple blog. Architecture inspired by AirFace / MobileNetv3 bottlenecks + MobileFaceNet-style global depthwise; ArcFace-style angular margin training — dim omitted.
pipeline.on_device_perf: Face embedding <4 ms on Apple Neural Engine (claimed 8× vs GPU equivalent).

evidence.claim: Face + upper-body dual embeddings; same-moment torso constraint; two-pass clustering; sparse coding assignment; dims not disclosed

primary_ablations.finding: Table 5 Embedding Dimensionality on hold-out VAL@FAR=1e-3 for NN1: 64D 86.8%±1.7; 128D 87.9%±1.9; 256D 87.7%±1.9; 512D 85.6%±2.0. Authors: differences statistically insignificant; larger may need more training. Chose 128D; float128 can quantize to 128-byte without accuracy loss.
primary_ablations.128_vs_512_same_backbone: In this controlled table, 128D slightly beats 512D (insignificant); does NOT show 128 underperforms 512.

primary_ablations.finding: Standard feature size set to 512 following prior work; x_i ∈ R^512 throughout. No dedicated 128/256/512/1024 accuracy ablation table found in the paper HTML.
Uses 512-D features at test (cosine on 512-D); no dim sweep vs 128.

Theoretical note: as #classes C grows relative to feature dim K, upper bound on cosine margin shrinks (C ≫ K hurts separability). Motivates sufficient dim for large-ID training sets but is not an empirical 128 vs 512 table.
No embedding-dim ablation; batch-size 128/256/512 studied instead.

industry_practice.sface_opencv: OpenCV zoo SFace = MobileFaceNet lineage commonly 128-D (user pipeline); zoo does not print dim in README; C++ wrapper forwards ONNX output as-is.
industry_practice.arcface_default: InsightFace/ArcFace ecosystem default 512-D for ResNet backbones.

does_128_underperform_512_same_backbone_.answer: No strong primary-source evidence that 128D systematically underperforms 512D at matched backbone+data. FaceNet's own ablation is the cleanest published same-backbone sweep and finds 128≈256≥512 within noise. Modern SOTA papers standardize on 512 without re-proving dim. Mobile models (MobileFaceNet/SFace) deliberately use 128 for efficiency and still hit high LFW-class scores. For large-ID galleries, CosFace theory suggests higher dim helps packing classes on the hypersphere — that is capacity/packing argument, not a measured 128-vs-512 delta.
does_128_underperform_512_same_backbone_.grade_note: Controlled 128 vs 512 underperformance claim: NOT CONFIRMED by ArcFace/MagFace/AdaFace primary tables; FaceNet contradicts it.

pgvector_ann_cost_scaling.storage: vector float32 storage ∝ N × d; halfvec halves bytes. HNSW index memory also scales with dim (graph stores full vectors or compressed depending on build).
pgvector_ann_cost_scaling.index_limits: pgvector HNSW/IVFFlat: vector up to 2000 dims; halfvec up to 4000.
pgvector_ann_cost_scaling.query_cost: Distance (L2/IP/cosine) is O(d) per candidate; higher d increases distance time and typically worsens constant-factor HNSW recall/latency tradeoff for fixed m/ef. Practical rule: 128→512 is ~4× vector bytes and ~4× distance math; index RAM and build time rise similarly.

q6_image_embedding_models.note: No major open whole-image embedder today has fully consented, commercially-clean, non-web training data at SOTA quality. "Clean training-data posture" is relative: prefer Apache/MIT weights + documented datasets; for strict compliance retrain on your consented/synthetic photo library (mirrors your face-pipeline plan).

summary_for_decision: OpenCV 5 (Jun 2026) is a real win for your ARM CPU path: new DNN engine + 80%+ ONNX + Arm KleidiCV/NEON, with YuNet 2026may dynamic-shape ONNX aimed at the 5.x ORT engine; FaceDetectorYN/SFace APIs look stable, but expect C++17, contrib moves, and CPU-only new engine until GPU lands. WIDER FACE is explicitly CC BY-NC-ND (HF: 4.0); zoo YuNet (MIT) and Paddle BlazeFace (Apache) still redistribute WIDER-trained weights — common practice but a residual commercial risk if you ship those weights; safer to retrain detector+embedder on synthetic/consented data and own the weights. VeriLook is a strong closed biometric (322 B proprietary templates, ~0.6 s PC extract, 40k match/s) with Linux ARM components, but DENY customer face-model retrain and DENY first-class raw vector→pgvector matching — templates store as blobs, scoring must go through their matcher. Apple Photos confirms dual face+torso embeddings with same-moment torso trust and two-pass clustering; dims unpublished. On embedding dim: FaceNet’s same-backbone ablation does not show 128≪512 (128 was best within noise); ArcFace/MagFace standardize on 512 without proving 128 fails; pgvector cost scales ~linear in d (storage, distance, HNSW RAM) — jump 128→512 mainly for large-ID packing headroom, not magic accuracy. For content-search embeddings prefer DINOv2 or SigLIP (Apache weights) over MobileCLIP (research-only weights) or LAION OpenCLIP if provenance sensitivity is high; none are fully "clean data," so consented retrain remains the cleanest commercial posture for both face and whole-image features on OCI A1.
